In summary, our research is concerned with

two main objectives: (a) to improve the classification performance of the state of the-art deep learning models by using image transforms and (b) to improve the generalization of the final classifier by using a committee of models trained with augmented data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have achieved state of the art melanoma detection results by exploring the combination of classical image transforms and expert knowledge based image warping, which are applied to artificially augment the ISBI training set.
we obtain a 0.94 Area Under the Curve (AUC) for melanoma classification, which is the best result reported for this dataset so far.
we have obtained a 5-fold improvement over the best published result on the test set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of classical image transforms and expert knowledge based image transforms can improve the performance of a deep learning melanoma classifier.

a combination of classical image processing transforms (such as contrast stretching, color balancing and histogram equalization) with image warping guided expert knowledge about the lesion shape, axis and color, improves the final classifier.
, in this particular problem, the combination of deep learning techniques with expert knowledge is a powerful tool that improves the classification performance.
